title: 2.1.4 Barley Production and Management
description: Barley: origin, malting, production practices, management and yield

questions.question: What is the scientific name of barley?
Where is barley believed to have originated?
options: The Asian continent, mainly China and India

questions.question: How do the growth requirements of barley compare with those of wheat?
options: Barley needs much lower temperatures than wheat
Barley grows only in lowland areas while wheat grows in the highlands
Barley grows on saline soils while wheat grows on loam soils

questions.question: How is barley used as human food and as livestock feed?
options: The grain is used as human food and the residue is used as livestock feed
The residue is used as human food and the grain is fed to animals
The grain is used as human food and the straw is used as fence material
Both the grain and the residue are used as human food
questions.correctAnswer: The grain is used as human food and the residue is used as livestock feed

questions.question: For what special purpose is barley used in industry?
options: Malting during the production of alcoholic beverages
questions.correctAnswer: Malting during the production of alcoholic beverages

questions.question: What is malting?
options: A process of controlled germination that produces enzymes converting cereal starch to sugars
A process of drying harvested grain in the sun
A process of boiling grain in water to produce porridge
A process of grinding grain into flour
questions.correctAnswer: A process of controlled germination that produces enzymes converting cereal starch to sugars

questions.question: What is done to the sugars produced during malting?
options: They are fermented to produce alcohol
They are dried to produce flour
They are stored to produce starch
questions.correctAnswer: They are fermented to produce alcohol

questions.question: At what altitude range does barley grow in Ethiopia?
Which soil is suitable for barley production?
options: Sandy soil with very low fertility

questions.question: How many times should the soil be cultivated before planting barley?
How is barley land preparation similar to wheat land preparation?
options: Both require soil to be cultivated 2 to 3 times before planting
Both require the soil to be cultivated 4 or 5 times and levelled
Both require only a single ploughing before planting
Both require the plot to be smoothed by driving animals on it
questions.correctAnswer: Both require soil to be cultivated 2 to 3 times before planting

questions.question: Which planting methods are used for barley?
When barley is planted in rows, what spacing is used between rows?
At what depth are barley seeds planted?
How much nitrogen do farmers usually apply per hectare for food barley production?
How much phosphorus do farmers usually apply per hectare for food barley production?
Why is the nitrogen application rate reduced for barley used for malting?
options: High levels of nitrogen application reduce the malt quality
High levels of nitrogen application damage the seeds
Nitrogen application makes malting barley lodge easily
Nitrogen attracts more insect pests during malting
questions.correctAnswer: High levels of nitrogen application reduce the malt quality

questions.question: What is the relationship between the weeds and diseases of barley and those of wheat?
options: Most weeds and diseases that affect wheat also affect barley
Barley is affected only by weeds and is free from wheat diseases
The weeds of barley are completely different from those of wheat
Barley diseases occur only in the lowlands while wheat diseases occur in the highlands
questions.correctAnswer: Most weeds and diseases that affect wheat also affect barley

questions.question: Which control measures are used for the weeds and diseases of barley?
options: Resistant varieties, crop rotation and changing planting times
Deep ploughing, earthing up and staking
questions.correctAnswer: Resistant varieties, crop rotation and changing planting times

questions.question: Which are the major insect pests affecting barley production?
options: Army worm, grasshopper and barley shoot fly
Maize stalk borer, aphids and weevil
African ball worm, aphids and bean fly
questions.correctAnswer: Army worm, grasshopper and barley shoot fly

questions.question: How long does barley usually take to mature?
What is the indicator that barley has reached maturity?
options: Drying and yellowing of the plant
The grains developing a black layer
The pods drying and changing colour from green to black
The grain moisture dropping to about $30$%
questions.correctAnswer: Drying and yellowing of the plant

questions.question: What is the national average yield of barley in Ethiopia?
Which nutrients is barley a source of?
options: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals and fibre

questions.question: Barley is a cereal crop whose seeds have which feature?
Which is the correct sequence of land preparation, planting and fertilization for food barley production?
options: Cultivate soil $2$ to $3$ times, sow broadcast or in rows $25$ cm apart at $5$ cm depth, apply $60$ kg nitrogen and $26$ kg phosphorus per hectare
Cultivate soil $4$ or $5$ times, sow in rows $20$ cm apart at $1$ cm depth, apply $45$ kg nitrogen and $25$ kg phosphorus per hectare
Cultivate soil once, sow in rows $75$ cm apart at $7$ cm depth, apply $41$ kg nitrogen and $20$ kg phosphorus per hectare
Cultivate soil $6$ times, sow at $2.5$ cm depth in rows $40$ cm apart, apply $32$ kg nitrogen and $10$ kg phosphorus per hectare
questions.correctAnswer: Cultivate soil $2$ to $3$ times, sow broadcast or in rows $25$ cm apart at $5$ cm depth, apply $60$ kg nitrogen and $26$ kg phosphorus per hectare
